findings.description: Regular expression denial of service (ReDoS) vulnerability in ANSI_CSI_RE pattern due to nested quantifiers on alternation group
findings.reasoning: The regex pattern contains a nested quantifier vulnerability: `((?:\\d|;)*)` applies a greedy `*` quantifier to an alternation group `(\\d|;)`. When processing malicious input with many digits or semicolons without a matching letter, the regex engine will experience catastrophic backtracking. The pattern is used in `write_and_convert()` method which processes user-controlled text input via `finditer()`, making it exploitable through specially crafted ANSI sequences.

evidence.code_context:
Line 78: ANSI_CSI_RE = re.compile('\001?\033\\[((?:\\d|;)*)([a-zA-Z])\002?')
Line 200: for match in self.ANSI_CSI_RE.finditer(text):
Line 195-210: write_and_convert() method processes user input with this regex
evidence.dataflow_analysis: User input flows from write() method parameter 'text' -> write_and_convert(text) -> ANSI_CSI_RE.finditer(text). The text parameter comes from stream.write() which can be called with arbitrary data.
evidence.notes: The vulnerable pattern has nested quantifiers: ((?:\d|;)*) where * is applied to an alternation group. This causes exponential backtracking when input contains many digits/semicolons without a terminating letter. Example: ESC[;;;;;;;;;;;; (many semicolons without letter) will cause severe performance degradation.

findings.description: Regular expression denial of service (ReDoS) vulnerability in ANSI_OSC_RE pattern due to greedy quantifier on negated character class
findings.reasoning: The regex pattern contains a greedy quantifier vulnerability: `([^\\a]*)` applies a greedy `*` quantifier to a negated character class. When processing malicious input with many non-BEL characters without a matching BEL character, the regex engine will experience catastrophic backtracking. The pattern is used in `convert_osc()` method which processes user-controlled text input via `finditer()`, making it exploitable through specially crafted ANSI sequences.

evidence.code_context:
Line 79: ANSI_OSC_RE = re.compile('\001?\033\\]([^\a]*)(\a)\002?')
Line 261: for match in self.ANSI_OSC_RE.finditer(text):
Line 255-270: convert_osc() method processes user input with this regex
evidence.dataflow_analysis: User input flows from write() method parameter 'text' -> write_and_convert(text) -> convert_osc(text) -> ANSI_OSC_RE.finditer(text). The text parameter comes from stream.write() which can be called with arbitrary data.
evidence.notes: The vulnerable pattern has a greedy quantifier on negated character class: ([^\a]*) where * is greedy. This causes exponential backtracking when input contains many non-BEL characters without a terminating BEL. Example: ESC]aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa (many 'a' characters without BEL) will cause severe performance degradation.
